## Abstract

We determine the asymptotic average sizes of the class numbers of indefinite binary quadratic forms when ordered by the sizes of their corresponding fundamental units. The proofs make use of the Selberg trace formula.


The results of this paper constitute part of the author's thesis, Stanford, 1980.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Abstract

We present a new algorithm that, given two matrices in GL⁡(𝑛,ℚ)\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Q}), decides if they are conjugate in GL⁡(𝑛,ℤ)\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z}) and, if so, determines a conjugating matrix. We also give an algorithm to construct a generating set for the centraliser in GL⁡(𝑛,ℤ)\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z}) of a matrix in GL⁡(𝑛,ℚ)\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Q}). We do this by reducing these problems, respectively, to the isomorphism and automorphism group problems for certain modules over rings of the form 𝒪𝐾⁡[𝑦]/(𝑦𝑙){\mathcal{O}}_{K}[y]/({y}^{l}), where 𝒪𝐾{\mathcal{O}}_{K} is the maximal order of an algebraic number field and 𝑙∈ℕl\in \mathbb{N}, and then provide algorithms to solve the latter. The algorithms are practical and our implementations are publicly available in Magma.

### Abstract

We present a new algorithm that, given two matrices in \mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Q}), decides if they are conjugate in \mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z}) and, if so, determines a conjugating matrix. We also give an algorithm to construct a generating set for the centraliser in \mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z}) of a matrix in \mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Q}). We do this by reducing these problems, respectively, to the isomorphism and automorphism group problems for certain modules over rings of the form {\mathcal{O}}_{K}[y]/({y}^{l}), where {\mathcal{O}}_{K} is the maximal order of an algebraic number field and l\in \mathbb{N}, and then provide algorithms to solve the latter. The algorithms are practical and our implementations are publicly available in Magma.

## Abstract

We obtain an asymptotic formula for the averages of class numbers of indefinite binary quadratic forms taken along certain polynomial sequences. It is found that along these sequences the class number is essentially as large as possible.

## Abstract

In [P. Sarnak, Class numbers of indefinite binary quadratic forms, J. Number Theory 15 (1982) 229–247], it was proved that the Selberg zeta function for is expressed in terms of the fundamental units and the class numbers of the primitive indefinite binary quadratic forms. The aim of this paper is to obtain similar arithmetic expressions of the logarithmic derivatives of the Selberg zeta functions for congruence subgroups of . As applications, we study the Brun–Titchmarsh type prime geodesic theorem and the asymptotic formula of the sum of the class number.
